<h1 align="center">CASTAWAY</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video, written out like a chiptune. It is mostly rests.</b><br>
  <sub>working title · in development, nothing published yet · an unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i></sub>
</p>

**Castaway** is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lo-fi streams: one young woman, one tiny island, one tall palm, a raft and a great deal of time. She idles, nodding to the music in her headphones. Every so often, something happens. A bottle she throws washes straight back. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A grey tabby arrives on a crate, climbs the palm, naps, and one day floats away again. It is always daytime.

Who turns up, and when, is [activities.toml](activities.toml), and it reads a lot like a tracker module. Every activity starts on the next bar of the music, so every gag lands on the beat. Lanes are channels (her, the cat, the turtle, the sea and sky, the shore, the kumara patch), so a ship can cross the horizon while she is busy with a coconut. Four timers pick from more than 90 activities, from *regular* (every 2 to 5 minutes) to *super rare* (every 3 to 6 hours, three at most). Written out one row per beat, ten hours is 48,000 rows, and the island plays about 200 notes in them. She is busy about a third of the time. The rest is rests.

The banner is minute 24 of the default run (seed 1992), as `tools/schedule.py` simulated it on 2026-10-01. At 0:24:09 she starts on a coconut, row `0C`. At 0:24:18, three bars later, a ship sets off across the horizon behind her, row `18`. The ship's entry in activities.toml lets it wait up to ten minutes for her to be busy: that is the `W0A` on its note. She does not look up. Headphones.

Every sound, more than 150 files so far, is synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, loops or recordings, so no third-party licence applies, and the tracker's sample channel has nothing to play. The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (ii-V-I-vi), 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, on electric piano, kalimba, soft drums and vinyl crackle, mixed to -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP. Levels are adjustable in master and per routine. Nobody has listened to any of it yet, so the tracker reserves judgement.

```sh
python tools/serve.py              # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
python tools/schedule.py           # validate the schedule, simulate 10 hours
python tools/render_demo.py --dev  # a dev reel of every activity, with a HUD
```

<sub>The page in <a href="web/index.html">web/index.html</a> previews live and exports a YouTube-ready MP4, frame-exact, encoded in the browser with WebCodecs; <a href="tools/serve.py">tools/serve.py</a> mixes in the sound and joins the two. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages. The default run is 10:00:00 on seed 1992: same seed, same video, event for event.</sub>

<details>
<summary><b>pattern 18</b>: how to read the screen up there</summary>

```text
 outrigger 0.92 · castaway.rig · frame 18 (minute 24), pattern loop on
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 1 row       one beat: 0.75 s at 80 BPM. a yellow row starts a bar (3 s)
 1 pattern   80 rows: one pass of the 60-second theme, one minute
 1 frame     one minute. ten hours is 600 frames, 000 to 257 in hex
 1 run       48,000 rows. the island plays about 200 notes in them
             (median of 200 simulated runs: about 155 regular, 30
             occasional, 13 rare, 2 super rare, plus chained follow-ups)
 1 cell      F-4   03    F     L11
             note  inst  vol   effect

 chip 1  ISLE-4   the island: lanes from activities.toml
    1 HER         her. one activity at a time
    2 SEA+SKY     the ship, the drone, the tour boat, the shark
    3 VISITORS    the cat's lane and the turtle's, sharing a channel
    4 SHORE       the tide, which takes sandcastles
 chip 2  LOFI-3   the theme, arranged from tools/make_audio.py
    5 KEYS        the chord as an arpeggio, strummed twice a bar
    6 BASS        root, fifth, and a lead-in under the next root
    7 BEAT        kick and snare; kick and rim in the breakdown
 chip 3  PCM-0    the sample channel. there are no samples. dots.

 island notes are the tier, tuned to F major:
    F-4 regular   A-4 occasional   C-5 rare   F-5 super rare
 effects:
    Lxx   lasts xx bars                     coconut: L11, 17 bars
    Wxx   may wait xx minutes for her       ship: W0A, ten minutes
          to be busy
    Gxx   note delay, xx ticks of 12        G06: the half-beat
    0xy   arpeggio                          the keys chord
    ===   note release

 orders, frames 14 to 1C: a lane gets a new pattern number whenever a
 minute's notes differ; 00 is a minute where nothing starts or stops.
 the theme channels play pattern 00 in all 600 frames, because the
 theme is one loop.

 keyboard: keys teal, bass amber, kalimba coral. the kalimba plays
 eighth notes, which a one-row-a-beat pattern cannot hold, so it
 lives down there.
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>module comments</b></summary>

```text
 composed by   a random number generator with good comic timing
 arranged by   tools/schedule.py, seed 1992
 voices by     tools/make_audio.py, out of arithmetic
 samples       none. the sample channel is there for symmetry
 length        10:00:00. there is no good bit to skip to. it is all
               the good bit
 thanks to     the coconut, for holding still; the ship, for its
               timing; the grey tabby, who comes and goes as it
               likes; the hermit crab, now wearing a coconut; and the
               kumara, which is growing as fast as it can
```

</details>

<sub>outrigger and its chips (ISLE-4, LOFI-3, PCM-0) do not exist. The screen is drawn after the modern multi-chip chiptune trackers and borrows none of their names or artwork. The schedule, the theme and minute 24 are real. Castaway is an unofficial remake inspired by <i>Johnny Castaway</i> (1992), which belongs to its owners.</sub>
